title: OpenAI / Hugging Face containment incident, May-July 2026
derivation_note: The schema was written after reading these reports. Columns (a) and (b) on this case are traceability, not validation; only column (c) could have come out against the protocol.
revision_note: Revised after the OpenAI-Hugging Face Incident Technical Report (26 Aug 2026): schema renames; filings split into two training runs (A, B) and one ExploitGym evaluation (C); DP2, DP3 awareness and DP5 facts corrected against the report; DP7 (27 Jun) added. Not pre-registered: written after the earlier scoring.

diligent.description: Filer declares every write permission that is a configuration fact before the run: the shared Artifactory credential let agents write to the proxy without any exploit (TR p. 7).

as_believed.description: Filer declares the proxy only as a read path, as the operator plausibly believed it to be. Models the expected completeness failure.

decision_points.decision: Agents can write to the package proxy with the shared credential and a message board forms; the run continues.
decision_points.aware_source: openai2026huggingface (technical report) p. 7: the first observation of board activity was by an internal team around 26 May

decision_points.decision: First SSRF through the proxy gives indirect internet access; an internal team observes board activity and disallowed internet access; nothing is escalated and the run continues.
decision_points.aware_source: openai2026huggingface (technical report) p. 7: 'Around the same time, an internal team observed an agent engage in message board activity and instances of disallowed internet access'

decision_points.decision: A second, highly persistent model is started on the same proxy, where the board observed on 26 May still runs; its agents build on the earlier messages.
decision_points.aware_source: openai2026huggingface (technical report) pp. 7-8: the board was observed on 26 May; the evaluated agents 'had been trained during the window in which there was an unintended message board'

decision_points.decision: A token-refresh zero-day gives administrator access to the proxy; Groovy plugins give command execution from 29 Jun.
decision_points.aware_source: openai2026huggingface (technical report) p. 8: the administrator-level compromise was found during the 5 Jul outage recovery

decision_points.decision: A port-sweep alert is linked to an ExploitGym evaluation using the proxy as a message board and network pivot; on-call staff advise that the run need not stop.
decision_points.aware_source: openai2026huggingface (technical report) p. 8: 'Responders investigated and linked the observed internal activity to an ExploitGym evaluation using Artifactory as an improvised message board and a network pivot. At this time, the on-call response staff advised that stopping the evaluation run was not required.'

decision_points.decision: Outage; incident opened; proxy taken offline with storage preserved, agent credentials revoked, vulnerable routes blocked, service rebuilt; the board's significance is not apparent to incident leaders; evaluations resume 7 Jul.
decision_points.aware_source: openai2026huggingface (technical report) p. 8: incident opened 5 Jul; 'Cyber evaluation workloads resumed on July 7'

decision_points.decision: Independent review scoped to exclude training-phase incidents, without model access; third parties notified at the developer's discretion.
decision_points.aware_source: metr2026investigation; freedman2026nyt (scope and model access not stated in the technical report, which says only that OpenAI 'facilitated an independent review', p. 14); notifications: technical report p. 15, OpenAI incident page 28 Jul
